title: PCA mapping and machine learning prioritize antiplasmodial chemotypes
summary: A PCA enrichment map and machine-learning virtual screening pipeline prioritized a commercial library for beta-haematin and parasite assays. The primary indexed paper reports several chemotypes evaluated for antiplasmodial activity, beta-haematin inhibition and haemozoin formation inhibition. This is an in-vitro campaign; results should not be conflated across assays or with clinical efficacy.
ai_technology: PCA enrichment mapping; support-vector machine classification; virtual screening

evidence.tested: PMC-hosted primary text reports PCA/ML screen and experimental parasite/haemozoin assays.
evidence.unknown: Exact structure-level overlaps with earlier UCT screens and detailed full-text quantitative results should be cross-checked before final prioritization.
evidence.ai_role: PCA map and classifier prioritize compounds for biochemical and cell assays.

source_review.scope: PMC-indexed primary article; PubMed primary metadata. Material checked for the specific claims stated in the record.
